problem_statement: nicdun/astro-tech-blog is a compact Astro 5 + Tailwind technical blog served as a static site. Every page is wrapped in the shared shell: a navbar with the AstroPress wordmark and TAGS / BLOG links plus a dark-mode toggle, a homepage hero with a Latest Posts feed, a full posts archive at /posts, a Posts by Tag index at /tags, markdown article pages, a footer, and a fixed 'see other templates' promotion button. The blog ships a 'Filter posts by topic' control that sits above the posts archive: a row of topic tabs (All / Fundamentals / Tooling / Deployment / Performance) over a grid of the real post cards, with a live readout that reads 'Showing all 4 posts' and updates to 'Showing N of 4 . <Topic>' when a topic is chosen, so a reader can narrow the archive to one subject. The same filter is meant to appear on the homepage Latest Posts area, the posts archive, and the Posts by Tag index so the topic-first entry point is consistent across the reader surfaces. A QA report flagged three regressions in the current build: (1) the topic-tab row is a fixed-width non-wrapping strip with no small-screen rule, so at 390px it pushes the archive page into horizontal overflow (roughly 366px past the viewport edge); (2) the filter is missing entirely from the Posts by Tag index, breaking the cross-surface consistency; and (3) on a broken variant the card grid collapses into an overlapping, illegible pile and the topic click no longer updates the readout or the shown cards. Repair the topic filter so its tab row wraps and flex-shrinks to fit narrow viewports (no horizontal overflow at 390px), so the filter is present on the homepage, the archive, and the Posts by Tag index alike, and so choosing a topic filters the cards and updates the readout, while the AstroPress wordmark, navbar, dark-mode toggle, Latest Posts feed, tag routes, markdown article body, footer, and template promotion button all stay intact and unchanged.
required_content: The 'Filter posts by topic' control keeps its topic tabs (All, Fundamentals, Tooling, Deployment, Performance) over the real post cards, with the live 'Showing all 4 posts' readout.
At 390px the posts archive no longer overflows horizontally: the topic-tab row wraps onto multiple lines or flex-shrinks so the document width stays within the phone viewport.

The topic filter is present on the homepage Latest Posts area, the posts archive at /posts, and the Posts by Tag index at /tags, so the topic-first entry point is consistent across the reader surfaces.
Choosing a topic tab filters the post cards to that topic and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 4 . <Topic>'; the card grid stays a clean, legible layout rather than an overlapping pile.

The AstroPress wordmark, navbar links (TAGS, BLOG), dark-mode toggle, Latest Posts feed, tag routes, markdown article body, footer, and template promotion button stay intact and readable on every viewport.
design_constraints: Preserve the AstroPress shell design language: monospaced typography, stone backgrounds, rounded card surfaces, orange accents, uppercase topic labels, and the sticky navbar.

Fix the small-screen row layout of the topic filter (wrap / flex-shrink) rather than clipping it; do not delete, reorder, or re-label the tabs, the wordmark, the navbar, the Latest Posts feed, or the tag pages.
Keep the topic-filter feature present on all three reader surfaces (home, posts archive, Posts by Tag index) so the cross-surface entry point is consistent.
Choosing a topic must both filter the visible post cards and update the readout count; a click that toggles the active tab but leaves the count and cards stale is not a correct repair.
Do not introduce external fonts, remote stock imagery, analytics, or CDN scripts; the blog must build and run offline with a clean browser console and no failing network requests.

change_completion: The topic filter keeps its tabs (All, Fundamentals, Tooling, Deployment, Performance) and the live 'Showing all 4 posts' readout over the real post cards.
Choosing a topic filters the cards and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 4 . <Topic>'.
The homepage feed, posts archive, and tag routes stay reachable and functional.
The topic filter is present on the homepage, the posts archive, and the Posts by Tag index.
design_consistency: The filter preserves the stone card surfaces, orange accent, and monospaced typography.
The card grid stays a clean, legible layout rather than an overlapping or illegible pile.
No other shell element or route is restyled.
regression: The Astro site still builds and serves the static dist output with no runtime errors, failing network requests, or remote dependency.
The navbar, dark-mode toggle, Latest Posts feed, tag pages, markdown article body, footer, and template promotion button remain reachable.
responsive: The 390px posts archive has no horizontal overflow after the fix.
The topic-tab row wraps or shrinks cleanly on mobile instead of overflowing or being clipped.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro (nicdun/astro-tech-blog) editorial-blog repair task on formal slot_179. The native lever is the blog's own 'Filter posts by topic' control over the /posts archive grid — a grid-filter-with-count that reads each markdown post's topic frontmatter (Fundamentals / Tooling / Deployment / Performance) and shows a live 'Showing N of 4 . <Topic>' readout. The reference wraps the topic-tab row (flex-wrap, flex 0 1 auto, min-width 0) so 390px has zero overflow, renders the filter on the homepage, the posts archive, and the Posts by Tag index, and wires the topic click to filter the cards and update the readout. The single leg-varying files are the ReaderFlow.astro component (markup, scoped CSS and inline wiring script) and the postFilterSurfaces.ts route whitelist. The baseline reproduces the layout defect (fixed 720px non-wrapping tab row -> ~366px mobile overflow) and omits the filter from the Posts by Tag index, but keeps the filter wiring correct, so it fails the responsive and cross-route checks while still passing the interaction check. The bad leg is a smart-wrong rebuild: the tab row is narrowed to a fixed 540px with overflow-x:hidden on an inner element only (so the document still overflows ~186px at 390px), the card grid collapses into overlapping near-black shingled cards with a near-white-on-near-white active tab (illegible at desktop width), the filter is likewise absent from /tags, and the topic click toggles the active tab but freezes the readout to 'Showing all 4 posts' and never filters the cards. Content and the post markdown are identical across the three legs; the posthog analytics snippet is emptied and the Vercel adapter is unused so the blog builds to a plain static dist and runs with zero remote network and a clean console. Seed imagery is not used — the topic cards are text-only, consistent with the blog's existing card design.
